citations.claim: light body gained +x velocity kick from rest
heavy body gained a smaller opposite kick, so momenta do not cancel and net momentum appears
both bodies started at rest so initial total momentum was zero

counterfactual.change: Set body 1 mass from 17.521047089796522 to 1.0 (equal masses); same dt/steps/G/positions. Predicts removal because asymmetric pairwise-force error scales with mass ratio and falls below tolerance when masses are equal.

explanation: From rest at step 0, one leapfrog step gives unequal-opposite kicks: light body dv~0.0574, heavy body dv~0.00295 (ratio ~19.5 vs mass ratio 17.5), leaving net momentum (0.00077,0.00569) and angular momentum 0.0416. Pairwise forces are not equal-and-opposite (e.g. sequential in-place evaluation using already-moved positions or mass-dependent force error), so Newton's 3rd law is violated and total momentum drifts. Equalizing masses removes the violation.
vision_note: Two bodies, a larger one above a smaller one, remain almost exactly in place between step 0 and step 1. No collision, wall hit, ejection, or other visible event occurs that could explain a momentum jump.
